transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-16
Time: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Julia Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ava Chen (Redwood CSM); Lena Morales (Acme ML Eng), Tom Wu (Acme Infra), Priya Kapoor (Acme Product)

Optional Summary: Quick review of the week's caching telemetry; agreed on canonicalization and a TTL experiment; next infra deep dive scheduled.

[00:00] Julia: okay uh let's get started i think we have about 45 minutes today, thanks everyone for joining
[00:08] Lena: thanks julia, yeah we wanted to make sure we had the hit-rate numbers ready and walk through the prompt strategy you recommended
[00:15] Samir: cool - quick agenda: 1) look at current KV cache (we'll call it K-V cash in the transcript, sorry) hit rates, 2) review the prefix normalization and canonicalization results, 3) decide on TTL and isolation, 4) next steps / owners
[00:30] Tom: sounds good. we had infra on standby for the tenant isolation questions
[00:36] Priya: and product wants to see what this means for latency and cost - the PM team has a budget threshold

[01:05] Samir: alright so first chart - overall KV cache hit rate across daily traffic. last week baseline before we applied prompt normalization was around 12% overall, after the first canonicalization pass it moved to about 48% for the high-frequency routes, so a big improvement but there's still a long tail
[01:22] Lena: wait, 48%? that seems higher than i expected, are we sure that's across all routes or just the top 10?
[01:28] Samir: good call - that's for the top 20 routes that have repetitive prompts, overall weighted average is ~33%, sorry i should've been precise, the top heavy ones got to roughly forty eight percent, overall thirty three
[01:38] Julia: and the top routes are the recommendation prompts and quick product detail queries, right?
[01:42] Samir: exactly. those are highly templated so canonicalization yields biggest gains there. the long-tail chatty prompts where users append small typos still kill hit-rate

[02:10] Lena: we attached a sample spreadsheet of prompt variants - see link in chat - about 500 variants for our checkout assistant alone
[02:17] Julia: yes we reviewed that, thank you. the approach we proposed was two fold: one, aggressive template canonicalization for known flows; two, a hashed-key approach removing user-specific slots (names, order ids) so the KV key maps to the intent+context fingerprint
[02:35] Tom: are we comfortable doing any PII stripping client-side vs server-side? security flagged that last week
[02:42] Ava: security note - Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for encrypting cache blobs in private deployments; for hosted we can use envelope encryption but we need to confirm scope. we'll follow up in the security doc share
[02:54] Priya: the product ask is: can we get hit-rate without increasing tail latency? like, if we do more normalization does that add CPU on the critical path?
[03:05] Samir: slight CPU overhead for canonicalization but it's negligible compared to model inference. the bigger risk is added pre-processing latency for very high qps routes; we can batch canonicalization or run async warmers in the pipeline

[05:10] Speaker 1: [crosstalk] um - sorry just to jump in - do we have numbers for how cache TTL affects freshness?
[05:18] Samir: yes, we ran a quick sensitivity sweep. TTL=10m gave best tradeoff for recommendations (cached embeddings/outputs stayed useful); TTL=1h increased hit-rate but we saw a decay in relevance for price-sensitive prompts. so recommendation from SE is 10m for recs, 30m-1h for static content like product descriptions
[05:40] Lena: ok that aligns with our expectations. can we do per-route TTLs? we need recs short, descriptions long
[05:46] Samir: yes per-route TTLs are supported in the runtime config, you can set per-model/per-route policies. just beware memory pressure if you set many long TTLs

[07:20] Julia: on cache keying we also suggested a prefix strategy: keep a short canonical prefix that captures intent and top-k context tokens, then append a blob-hash of the rest. that gives us better prefix/KV hits for repeated fronts
[07:35] Lena: local question: some of our prompts include session-specific random tokens - does the hash approach need us to strip random seeds?
[07:42] Samir: yes strip any non-semantic randomizers - that's part of template normalization. we provided a regex set in last week's notes, looks like some variants slipped through

[09:15] Tom: infra question: are we using shared cache across tenants or tenant-scoped caches? the shared cache was cheaper but security wanted per-tenant isolation
[09:24] Ava: tradeoffs: shared cache has higher hit-rate due to cross-tenant common prompts but per-tenant isolates data for compliance. Redwood supports both; for Private you can run per-tenant namespaces in the cache and still get reasonable hit rates if you warm them
[09:40] Tom: warming is the key - can we run a warming job at deployment to prefill common keys?
[09:45] Samir: yes we can run a proactive warmer. we can also snapshot common top-k keys from the baseline traces and seed them into the cache on startup

[11:10] Priya: about metrics - can you send us a breakdown by prompt-cluster and latency percentile? we need 95th pct before/after canonicalization to present to execs
[11:18] Julia: absolutely. Samir will share the dashboard and a CSV export of the raw samples

[12:00] Samir: quick note on eviction: runtime uses LRU by default but you can plug a cost-based eviction policy. for our workloads, LRU + size-based caps worked well but if you have very large static documents you might want a pinlist for those keys
[12:18] Lena: pinlist would help for product descriptions so they don't churn out of cache

[14:05] Speaker 2: there's some noise in the logs where the service mis-labeled some keys as 'prefix-??' - might be an older agent version
[14:12] Samir: yes that was fixed in 0.9.3 of the runtime; make sure staging is on the latest image. older agent emits slightly different key format which fragments hit-rate

[15:40] Lena: ok, we ran the test 24-hour replay on staging with canonicalization and saw average latency drop 13% and cost per 1k tokens down by ~8% - rough numbers
[15:50] Priya: that's promising. can we translate cost reduction to our monthly spend?
[15:54] Julia: we estimated for Acme's traffic profile that 8% token cost reduction maps to ~$7k/month saving on current hosted run-rate, but with dedicated reserved capacity that could be larger due to improved utilization

[18:00] Tom: question, does this affect model selection? like, if caching reduces load, can we move to a slightly larger context model or a cheaper model tier?

[18:10] Samir: it opens options. if cache hit rates are high for prompt-heavy routes you can push more work to cached outputs and use smaller models for reactive fallbacks. we have routing policies that pick model variants by route and SLOs

[20:05] Lena: we still saw a cold-start problem for new users - first few queries are always misses and that's a UI experience issue. any ideas?
[20:12] Samir: warmer + synthetic seed prompts for new user cohorts, or prefetch caches when you detect a new session with predictable flows. also reduce cold latency by keeping a small hot-cache reserved per-region

[22:30] Ava: security checklist reminder: we need to confirm KMS key rotation policy, audit logs for cache reads/writes, and whether cache access shows up in our SIEM. we'll drop the security doc in the portal after this call

[24:00] Julia: recap - agreed experiments: 1) apply stronger canonicalization to top 500 prompt variants (Lena), 2) staging push of updated cache keys and per-route TTLs (Samir), 3) infra to confirm per-tenant isolation options and KMS scope (Tom), 4) Redwood to share dashboard and CSV (Samir/Julia)

[24:40] Lena: timeline from Acme: we'll run the canonicalized workload in staging by end of next week and report numbers. good to have infra deep dive the week after

[26:00] Speaker 1: random minor note - sometimes the transcript shows 'red wood' instead of 'Redwood' - not important but lol
[26:05] Julia: yeah that's the transcription; ignore typos

[27:10] Samir: a couple implementation specifics: we recommend hashing prompt body EXCEPT whitelisted slots (order_id, user_name removed), using a salted hash with tenant id for shared cache to avoid cross-tenant key collisions, and keeping prefix length to first 40 tokens for the prefix index

[28:00] Tom: salted hash sounds fine - just confirm the salt isn't customer secret, more like a namespace id? will that complicate KMS?
[28:08] Ava: salt is a namespace id, encryption is separate. KMS is used to encrypt cache payloads at rest, not the hashing step

[30:20] Priya: any concerns about evaluation/regression - how do we ensure canonicalization doesn't regress quality for edge cases?
[30:28] Samir: we'll run A/B with a sample set of ground-truth prompts and monitor quality metrics (BLEU-ish and manual evals for conversational responses). Redwood's rollout supports canary percentages with automatic fallback if quality drops

[32:50] Lena: what about prompt reuse strategy for multi-turn sessions? sometimes users repeat earlier system instructions which we currently include verbatim in the prompt

[32:58] Samir: for multi-turn, keep a compact session summary token instead of the full prior system prompt when length is high; that's part of the prefix strategy - summary plus last N messages hashed into a session fingerprint

[34:40] Julia: ok to surface an action item: Samir to share the config snippet for per-route TTLs and the canonicalization regex set
[34:48] Samir: noted, will share by EOD Friday (2026-06-18)

[36:10] Tom: one last infra thing - if we go per-tenant caches, what's the expected memory delta? ballpark numbers?
[36:20] Samir: depends on TTL and traffic; estimate for Acme's 95th percentile traffic a ~25% memory bump if you switch from fully shared to soft-isolated namespaces with pinlist enabled. we'll give a more precise number after staging metrics

[38:00] Priya: next meeting cadence - keep weekly for now until the main experiments finish
[38:06] Julia: agree weekly, same time.

[39:00] Julia: final recap for notes and owners: Samir - push patch to staging, share dashboard CSV and TTL config; Lena - produce canonicalization list and run staging replay; Tom - confirm VPC/KMS scope and plan for deep dive; Ava - drop security/compliance doc; Julia - follow up on cost impact estimate and coordinate next infra deep dive
[39:25] Lena: okay noted, thanks everyone
[39:30] Tom: thanks, bye
[39:33] Priya: bye bye
[39:35] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with the links and the CSV

End of transcript.

References/Links mentioned: 
- prompt-variants.xlsx (shared in chat)
- staging-dashboard.kibana (link)
